data.name: release-machinery-survey
data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).
11. Check flutter_app/lib for how the app displays its version (package_info_plus? hardcoded?).

Report as a structured list with file:line and short quotes. Do NOT modify anything.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

printf '## %s\n\n%s\n\n' "$version" "$section" > "$changelog.new"
# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
  skip { next }
  { print }
' "$changelog" >> "$changelog.new"
mv "$changelog.new" "$changelog"

data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? 6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).

9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CHANGELOG size guard (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds its hard content cap — `Message from server:
# CHANGELOG.md exceeds the maximum content length (262144 bytes)`. v1.0.538
# died at `dart pub publish` AFTER the tag + GitHub release existed, so the
# version never reached pub.dev. The changelog is append-only by convention
# and the auto-release grows it near-daily; nothing bounded it before this
# guard.
#
# Callers (keep both wired — test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart asserts the
# wiring):
#   - scripts/auto_release.sh   — BEFORE the bump commit/tag (pre-tag
#     fast-fail: the push is what fires tag_release + the publish job);
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml `publish` job gate — BEFORE staging/upload
#     (the server reject is the worst possible discovery point).
#
# Usage: check_changelog_size.sh [file] [cap_bytes]
#   file  defaults to CHANGELOG.md (the file pub packs);
#   cap   defaults to 262144 (the pub.dev cap) — strict less-than; the
#         override exists for tests.
#
# Exit 0 = under the cap. Exit 1 = missing file or size >= cap, with a
# ::error:: annotation naming the fix (archive the tail).
set -euo pipefail

file="${1:-CHANGELOG.md}"
cap="${2:-262144}"

if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "::error::check_changelog_size.sh: $file does not exist — a release without a changelog is a broken release (gh-1452)."

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────

#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }

Required changes:

1. runVerify sandbox (~lines 237-380): the script now derives the version under test from the LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v*'` — real git call against the sandbox's real bare origin, so no shim needed for it) instead of reading pubspec.yaml. Keep the pubspec.yaml seed ONLY for the publish_to:none check. The `version` param semantics change: the fixture's tag v[version] now DEFINES the version (previously the pubspec did). Remove now-dead fixture params: bumpSubject/bumpAge/commitsOnTop (the 'bump on main' concept is gone). Keep: tagPresent, tagAge, publishToNone, runsJson, secondReadJson, conclusion, rerunToSuccess, lsremoteFailFirst (still meaningful — a transient ls-remote failure), firstViewJson, extraEnv. Update the sandbox doc comment.

2. DELETE the tests for states that no longer exist (the tag is the version — it exists on the remote by construction):
   - 'tag-pending', 'tag-pending-buried' (~734-767)
   - 'old-bump-pending' (~820), 'untagged-no-bump' (~830)
   - 'tag-appears-mid-wait' (~983), 'appear-wait-lapse' (~998)
   - The 'AC3 — tag_release.sh pins the bump commit' group (~1054-1174) — the script is DELETED from the repo; delete the whole group AND the runTagRelease sandbox + TagReleaseRun class (~383-535) including its flutter stub usage.
   Also remove 'never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)' expectations anywhere.

3. KEEP and verify still-passing: the release-in-flight classifications (run list empty + young tag grace, starved-run, expired-no-run → 'never triggered ... no run registered past the grace window', success-but-behind, rerun-recovers, repushed-old-tag), the #1368 push-twin group, 'verify — unchanged paths' (up-to-date, private, e2-current-tag-only).

4. plan gate group (~1294-end): daily_plan.sh re-arm now compares pub.dev served vs the LATEST LOCAL TAG (git tag --sort=-v:refname), and emits pubspec_version = latest tag version (no tag → 'pubspec_version=' empty-ish? read the script: `echo "pubspec_version=${latest_tag#v}"` — with latest_tag empty that prints the literal string; check the script). Rework runPlan fixtures: the sandbox seeds local tags instead of a pubspec version; the re-arm test 'main quiet but pub.dev behind the latest tag → changed=true'; add a 'no tags → no re-arm (changed stays false)'; the pubspec_version output assertion = latest tag version. Read the new scripts/daily_plan.sh carefully and pin its actual behavior.

5. Wiring group (~1175-1293): update pins: 'Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version' step name in daily-publish.yml is KEPT (do not change the workflow — the step name must keep matching); the script it runs is still scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh; remove any pins on scripts/tag_release.sh or the release-tag job; add pins asserting daily-publish.yml's verify step still routes through scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh and ci.yml has NO release-tag job.

6. Grep the whole file for stale references: 'tag_release', 'release-tag', 'chore(release)', 'bump' and fix every pin/comment to match the new reality.

Run `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart` until fully green. Report: what you changed, test result summary.

data.name: release-machinery-survey
data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────

#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;

section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1

# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section

# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }

data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

printf '## %s\n\n%s\n\n' "$version" "$section" > "$changelog.new"
# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
  skip { next }
  { print }
' "$changelog" >> "$changelog.new"
mv "$changelog.new" "$changelog"

# gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds its
# hard 262144-byte content cap. The repo file is capped by
# scripts/check_changelog_size.sh at authoring time; the STAGED file gets
# the same cap enforced HERE (it just grew by a fresh section) — trim the
# oldest sections until it fits. The trimmed tail is not lost: the repo

data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.

Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).

7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').

9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.

blocks.text:
The stamp works: the Unreleased body was folded under `## 1.0.550`, the staged Unreleased header dropped. One wrinkle: there's a blank-line gap (`## 1.0.550\n- gh-1522...`) — release_notes.sh output starts with a blank line? The awk section extraction picks up leading blank lines of the section. Minor cosmetic. Let me improve: the stamp script could strip leading blank lines from section. Actually the `## Unreleased\n- gh-1522...` — awk prints lines after the header including the blank line. Then printf '## %s\n%s\n' adds its own blank. Result: double blank. Let me fix by trimming leading blank lines of $section in the stamp script:

section="$(printf '%s' "$section" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//')" — but that would strip leading whitespace of first content line, fine for markdown bullets? sed '1{/^[[:space:]]*$/d}' loop... simpler: use a small awk to drop leading blank lines:

section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF{p=1} p')"

That drops leading blank lines. Trailing: release_notes awk already may include trailing newline; printf adds \n. OK.

Also check the cap-trim branch: hard to test quickly with a 262KB staged changelog — I can test by invoking with a tiny cap override? The stamp script hardcodes cap 262144 in the python. # ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

printf '## %s\n\n%s\n\n' "$version" "$section" > "$changelog.new"
# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
  skip { next }
  { print }
' "$changelog" >> "$changelog.new"
mv "$changelog.new" "$changelog"

data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).
11. Check flutter_app/lib for how the app displays its version (package_info_plus? hardcoded?).

Report as a structured list with file:line and short quotes. Do NOT modify anything.

blocks.text:
The staged file lost the `## 9.9.9` section AND the `# Changelog` header, and the newest kept section is 1.0.3?? The sections are ordered 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6 — ascending, and 9.9.9 missing entirely.

Bugs:
1. The trim's `kept` list: iterating `reversed(versions)` — versions order in file: [9.9.9, 1.0.6, 1.0.5, 1.0.4, 1.0.3, 1.0.2, 1.0.1]. reversed → [1.0.1, 1.0.2, ... 9.9.9]. It keeps from the OLDEST until cap! My comment said "newest first" but reversed(versions) with versions in file order (newest first, since we prepend) means reversed = oldest first. Kept = oldest 4 (1.0.1? no—1.0.3..1.0.6 shown). Then `"".join(reversed(kept))` re-reverses → 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6 ascending. And 9.9.9 was dropped because cap filled before reaching it. WRONG — must keep the NEWEST.

Fix: iterate `versions` directly (already newest-first), keep until cap:
```
for s in versions:  # newest first
    b = len(s)
    if kept and size + b >= cap: break
    kept.append(s); size += b
...
write head + "".join(kept)  # already newest-first
```

Wait, why did 1.0.1/1.0.2 not appear? kept=[1.0.1] then... hmm sizes: each section ~ (800 bullets * 22 chars) + 400 x = ~57KB+40KB = 57.6KB? Actually 800*22 = 17.6KB + 40KB = 57.6KB. head tiny. kept: 1.0.1 (57.6K), 1.0.2 (115K), 1.0.3 (173K), 1.0.4 (230K), 1.0.5: 288K ≥ cap → break. kept=[1.0.1..1.0.4], reversed → 1.0.4,1.0.3,1.0.2,1.0.1?? But the file shows 1.0.3..1.0.6. Hmm, that doesn't match either.

Wait — where's ## 9.9.9? Not in file at all. And sections present: 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6 — the NEWEST four, ascending. So kept must have been [1.0.6, 1.0.5, 1.0.4, 1.0.3] then reversed → [1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6]. That means `versions` order was OLDEST first — i.e. the input file's section order... 

OH WAIT. I see it. The input /tmp/fake-stage/CHANGELOG.md I generated: header, ## Unreleased, then `for in 1 2 3 4 5 6` ascending — so OLDEST first in my fixture (my generator wrote 1.0.1 first). But that's just my fixture being unrealistic (real changelog has newest first after prepends). But regardless of fixture order, the algorithm must keep the NEWEST BY VERSION. With fixture order oldest-first, `reversed(versions)` = newest-first iteration → kept=[1.0.6,1.0.5,1.0.4,1.0.3]... then join reversed → oldest-first-of-kept = 1.0.3..1.0.6. That matches the output!

And `## 9.9.9` — the split: `re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)` — the prepended section was written via printf '## %s\n%s\n' — so text starts "# Changelog\n## 9.9.9\n- Fresh curated note\n..." wait NO. Look at my stamp script:

awk ... >> "$changelog.new"
```

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):

#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`

#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

printf '## %s\n\n%s\n\n' "$version" "$section" > "$changelog.new"
# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }

It keeps from the OLDEST until cap! My comment said "newest first" but reversed(versions) with versions in file order (newest first, since we prepend) means reversed = oldest first. Kept = oldest 4 (1.0.1? no—1.0.3..1.0.6 shown). Then `"".join(reversed(kept))` re-reverses → 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6 ascending. And 9.9.9 was dropped because cap filled before reaching it. WRONG — must keep the NEWEST.

for s in versions:  # newest first

#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.

# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }

#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.

# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Deferred store-appearance check (gh-1041) — the IO half of the goal.
#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.
#
# Decisions live in flutter_app/fastlane/store_appearance.rb (plain-ruby
# tested); this script is transport + gh issue lifecycle only. Stdlib only —
# runs on the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Env (all store endpoints overridable for fake-endpoint IT):
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PUBDEV_BASE   default https://pub.dev/api
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_ASC_BASE      default https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_BASE     default https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_TOKEN_URL default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_NOW / _SINCE / _HORIZON_MINUTES / _RUN_URL   (tests/ops)
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_DRY_RUN=1     compute + print actions, no gh writes
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT, PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON

#   PUBDEV_PACKAGE, DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
#
# One python step does the whole staged edit: prepend the generated section
# under the file's `# Changelog` preamble (file order is newest-first — the
# stamp prepends), drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became
# the tag's section or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the
# published artifact never shows an Unreleased section), and keep only what
# fits under pub.dev's cap, newest first — the fresh tag section always
# survives. The trimmed tail is not lost: the repo file (git) and
# CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md carry the full history.
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
FA_SECTION="$section" FA_VERSION="$version" FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

cap = 262144
path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
version = os.environ["FA_VERSION"]
section = os.environ["FA_SECTION"].strip("\n")

text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
preamble = parts[0]
versions = [
    s
    for s in parts[1:]
    if s.startswith("## ")
    and not re.match(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", s.split("\n", 1)[0])
]
new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"
size = len((preamble + new).encode("utf-8"))
kept = []
for s in versions:  # file order: newest first (the stamp prepends)
    b = len(s.encode("utf-8"))
    if kept and size + b >= cap:
        break
    kept.append(s)
    size += b
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(preamble + new + "".join(kept))
PY

# gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds its
# hard 262144-byte content cap — the guard above already trims to fit, so a
# failure here means even the preamble + the single fresh section is over
# (pathological); a second pass keeping ONLY the fresh section is the last
# resort before the loud fail.

  echo "staged CHANGELOG still over the pub.dev cap — keeping only the fresh section"
  FA_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

path = os.environ["FA_CHANGELOG"]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(parts[0] + parts[1])
PY
  bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog"
}

# ── 2. Generate + prepend the tag's changelog section ──────────────────────
# Preference order (mirrors scripts/release_notes.sh, extended gh-1522):
#   a. a curated `## <version>` section already in the repo CHANGELOG.md;
#   b. the curated `## Unreleased` body, folded under `## <version>`
#      (the release "moves Unreleased into the tag's section AT STAGE
#      TIME — not in-repo", gh-1522 §2);
#   c. generated conventional-commit bullets since the previous tag
#      (release_notes.sh fallback, RELEASE_NOTES_MAX capped).
section="$(bash "$repo_root/scripts/release_notes.sh" "$version" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$section" ]; then
  echo "::error::could not generate a changelog section for v$version"
  exit 1
fi
# Drop leading blank lines (the awk section extraction carries the blank
# line right under the section header) so the staged section is tight.
section="$(printf '%s\n' "$section" | awk 'NF { p = 1 } p')"

printf '## %s\n\n%s\n\n' "$version" "$section" > "$changelog.new"
# Drop the staged `## Unreleased` header+body (it became the tag's section
# or stays in-repo curation for the NEXT release — the published artifact
# never shows an Unreleased section).
awk '
  BEGIN { skip = 0 }
  /^## Unreleased[ \t]*$/ { skip = 1; next }
  skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
  skip { next }
  { print }
' "$changelog" >> "$changelog.new"
mv "$changelog.new" "$changelog"

# gh-1452: pub.dev server-rejects an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds its
# hard 262144-byte content cap. The repo file is capped by

# the same cap enforced HERE (it just grew by a fresh section) — trim the
# oldest sections until it fits. The trimmed tail is not lost: the repo
# file (git) and CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md carry the full history.
bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog" || {
  echo "staged CHANGELOG over the pub.dev cap — trimming oldest staged sections"
  STAGED_CHANGELOG="$changelog" python3 - <<'PY'
import os
import re

path = os.environ["STAGED_CHANGELOG"]
cap = 262144
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
sections = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
head, versions = sections[0], [s for s in sections[1:] if s.startswith("## ")]
# Always keep the newest section plus whatever fits under the cap.
kept = []
size = len(head.encode("utf-8"))
for s in reversed(versions):
    b = len(s.encode("utf-8"))
    if kept and size + b >= cap:
        break
    kept.append(s)
    size += b
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(head + "".join(reversed(kept)))
PY
  bash "$repo_root/scripts/check_changelog_size.sh" "$changelog"
}

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the

# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Deferred store-appearance check (gh-1041) — the IO half of the goal.
#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.
#
# Decisions live in flutter_app/fastlane/store_appearance.rb (plain-ruby
# tested); this script is transport + gh issue lifecycle only. Stdlib only —
# runs on the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Env (all store endpoints overridable for fake-endpoint IT):
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PUBDEV_BASE   default https://pub.dev/api
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_ASC_BASE      default https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_BASE     default https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_TOKEN_URL default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_NOW / _SINCE / _HORIZON_MINUTES / _RUN_URL   (tests/ops)
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_DRY_RUN=1     compute + print actions, no gh writes
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT, PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
#   TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, IOS_BUNDLE_ID, PLAY_PACKAGE_NAME, PLAY_TRACK,
#   PUBDEV_PACKAGE, DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE
#
# Usage: ruby scripts/store_appearance_check.rb [--only testflight|play|pubdev]

require "json"
require "net/http"
require "tempfile"
require "uri"

S = StoreAppearance

  value.empty? ? default : value
end

assignee = env("DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE", "ai-teammate")

only = nil

Rework test/release_flow_race_test.dart for the gh-1522 tag-only release flow. ONLY edit test/release_flow_race_test.dart.

Read the current file, the new scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh, scripts/daily_plan.sh, and .github/workflows/daily-publish.yml first.

Required changes:

1. runVerify sandbox (~lines 237-380): the script now derives the version under test from the LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v*'` — real git call against the sandbox's real bare origin, so no shim needed for it) instead of reading pubspec.yaml. Keep the pubspec.yaml seed ONLY for the publish_to:none check. The `version` param semantics change: the fixture's tag v[version] now DEFINES the version (previously the pubspec did). Remove now-dead fixture params: bumpSubject/bumpAge/commitsOnTop (the 'bump on main' concept is gone). Keep: tagPresent, tagAge, publishToNone, runsJson, secondReadJson, conclusion, rerunToSuccess, lsremoteFailFirst (still meaningful — a transient ls-remote failure), firstViewJson, extraEnv. Update the sandbox doc comment.

2. DELETE the tests for states that no longer exist (the tag is the version — it exists on the remote by construction):
   - 'tag-pending', 'tag-pending-buried' (~734-767)
   - 'old-bump-pending' (~820), 'untagged-no-bump' (~830)
   - 'tag-appears-mid-wait' (~983), 'appear-wait-lapse' (~998)
   - The 'AC3 — tag_release.sh pins the bump commit' group (~1054-1174) — the script is DELETED from the repo; delete the whole group AND the runTagRelease sandbox + TagReleaseRun class (~383-535) including its flutter stub usage.
   Also remove 'never triggered (no tag and no chore(release) bump on main)' expectations anywhere.

3. KEEP and verify still-passing: the release-in-flight classifications (run list empty + young tag grace, starved-run, expired-no-run → 'never triggered ... no run registered past the grace window', success-but-behind, rerun-recovers, repushed-old-tag), the #1368 push-twin group, 'verify — unchanged paths' (up-to-date, private, e2-current-tag-only).

4. plan gate group (~1294-end): daily_plan.sh re-arm now compares pub.dev served vs the LATEST LOCAL TAG (git tag --sort=-v:refname), and emits pubspec_version = latest tag version (no tag → 'pubspec_version=' empty-ish? read the script: `echo "pubspec_version=${latest_tag#v}"` — with latest_tag empty that prints the literal string; check the script). Rework runPlan fixtures: the sandbox seeds local tags instead of a pubspec version; the re-arm test 'main quiet but pub.dev behind the latest tag → changed=true'; add a 'no tags → no re-arm (changed stays false)'; the pubspec_version output assertion = latest tag version. Read the new scripts/daily_plan.sh carefully and pin its actual behavior.

5. Wiring group (~1175-1293): update pins: 'Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version' step name in daily-publish.yml is KEPT (do not change the workflow — the step name must keep matching); the script it runs is still scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh; remove any pins on scripts/tag_release.sh or the release-tag job; add pins asserting daily-publish.yml's verify step still routes through scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh and ci.yml has NO release-tag job.

6. Grep the whole file for stale references: 'tag_release', 'release-tag', 'chore(release)', 'bump' and fix every pin/comment to match the new reality.

Run `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart` until fully green. Report: what you changed, test result summary.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Deferred store-appearance check (gh-1041) — the IO half of the goal.
#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.
#
# Decisions live in flutter_app/fastlane/store_appearance.rb (plain-ruby
# tested); this script is transport + gh issue lifecycle only. Stdlib only —
# runs on the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Env (all store endpoints overridable for fake-endpoint IT):
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PUBDEV_BASE   default https://pub.dev/api
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_ASC_BASE      default https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_BASE     default https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_TOKEN_URL default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_NOW / _SINCE / _HORIZON_MINUTES / _RUN_URL   (tests/ops)
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_DRY_RUN=1     compute + print actions, no gh writes
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT, PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
#   TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, IOS_BUNDLE_ID, PLAY_PACKAGE_NAME, PLAY_TRACK,

data.name: release-machinery-survey
data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).
11. Check flutter_app/lib for how the app displays its version (package_info_plus? hardcoded?).

Report as a structured list with file:line and short quotes. Do NOT modify anything.

data.name: release-machinery-survey
data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).
11. Check flutter_app/lib for how the app displays its version (package_info_plus? hardcoded?).

Report as a structured list with file:line and short quotes. Do NOT modify anything.

data.name: release-machinery-survey
data.task:
Survey the release machinery in this repo and report precisely:

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — find the `release` job (runs scripts/auto_release.sh) and `release-tag` job (runs scripts/tag_release.sh). Quote their step lists (what token, env, trigger conditions). Also whether anything else in ci.yml references chore(release) or the bump commit.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` and `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — quote the publish job(s): trigger (tags?), the stage step (stage_publish_package.sh), the dart pub publish step (OIDC?), any version checks. Report how VERSION is derived (git tag --sort=-v:refname?).
3. `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/release-appstore.yml` — report each job's `Derive version` step (exact commands), and how version/build-number reach the flutter build / fastlane invocation. Note every place a version string flows (env vars like BUILD_NAME/BUILD_NUMBER, flutter build --build-name flags, fastlane lanes).
4. `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` — quote `def store_pubspec_version` (line ~57) and every call site context: what env vars (BUILD_NAME etc.) they fall back to.
5. `bin/fah.dart` / `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` — how does `fa --version` print the version? Which package reads pubspec version at runtime? Search for `packageVersion` / `--version` handling / any pubspec version reading code in lib/. Also find app-version displays in the TUI/app footers that resolve the package version (search lib/ and flutter_app/lib for version display code, e.g. footer, status bar, about screen).
6. `scripts/release_notes.sh` — what it reads (CHANGELOG sections? git log?).
7. Check `docs/` for a release-process / pub.dev release checklist doc (ls docs/, grep for 'release checklist' / 'pub.dev').
8. Check AGENTS.md for the release section (grep -n 'release' AGENTS.md around the release-process paragraph) — quote it.
9. `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` — what it checks and where it's called from.
10. Any other workflows referencing `version:` in pubspec.yaml or deriving versions (grep -rn 'sort=-v:refname' .github/ scripts/).
11. Check flutter_app/lib for how the app displays its version (package_info_plus? hardcoded?).

Report as a structured list with file:line and short quotes. Do NOT modify anything.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby

# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Deferred store-appearance check (gh-1041) — the IO half of the goal.
#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.
#
# Decisions live in flutter_app/fastlane/store_appearance.rb (plain-ruby

# runs on the runner's stock ruby.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

# Deferred store-appearance check (gh-1041) — the IO half of the goal.
#
# A store SUBMIT that returned green success is final: this job — not the
# submit legs — owns APPEARANCE. Scheduled 120 min after the daily publish
# legs (owner ruling 2026-09-28), it re-checks the three stores READ-ONLY
# (ASC API / Play API / pub.dev API, the legs' own credentials — I3) for the
# expected version resolved from the repo's tag/version file, then:
#
#   * all present   → one green-summary comment on the day's [daily-publish]
#                     stubs (once per day per stub — idempotency, REG);
#   * absent past the horizon (default 120 min) → EXACTLY ONE stub per store
#                     (label store-appearance-check), updated in place by
#                     later checks until the version appears or rolls over;
#   * API error     → reported, never stubbed (noise guard) — the run goes
#                     red but files nothing.
#
# Decisions live in flutter_app/fastlane/store_appearance.rb (plain-ruby
# tested); this script is transport + gh issue lifecycle only. Stdlib only —
# runs on the runner's stock ruby.
#
# Env (all store endpoints overridable for fake-endpoint IT):
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PUBDEV_BASE   default https://pub.dev/api
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_ASC_BASE      default https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_BASE     default https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_PLAY_TOKEN_URL default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_NOW / _SINCE / _HORIZON_MINUTES / _RUN_URL   (tests/ops)
#   STORE_APPEARANCE_DRY_RUN=1     compute + print actions, no gh writes
#   APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT, PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
#   TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP, IOS_BUNDLE_ID, PLAY_PACKAGE_NAME, PLAY_TRACK,

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

The release job looks correct. One issue: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` on a dry-run dispatch — the mint is skipped, output is empty → GH_TOKEN empty. auto_release.sh dry-run exits before gh release create, so fine.

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}

          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
