  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'

          if [ -x "${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa" ]; then
            fa_path="${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin/fa"

          if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pin_release.sh — advance the `vpinned` release marker to a freshly signed
# tag. PURE RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION: no commits, no pushes, no
# working-tree mutation — the marker lives entirely in GitHub Releases.
# The tag-scoped install-pin-bump CI job runs this after release-provenance
# published SHA256SUMS(.sig) for the tag.
#
# Trust model (SEC-07 #795): the marker is only a POINTER. Before it moves,
# the target release must pass check_install_pin.sh (signature verifies
# against the committed trust anchor + full platform coverage); after it
# moves, the gate runs again against the marker itself. A compromised
# marker therefore degrades to a DoS (install fails closed), never to a
# bad binary — the installer's embedded anchor is the real trust root.

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0

# pin_release.sh — advance the `vpinned` release marker to a freshly signed
# tag. PURE RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION: no commits, no pushes, no
# working-tree mutation — the marker lives entirely in GitHub Releases.
# The tag-scoped install-pin-bump CI job runs this after release-provenance
# published SHA256SUMS(.sig) for the tag.
#
# Trust model (SEC-07 #795): the marker is only a POINTER. Before it moves,

# against the committed trust anchor + full platform coverage); after it
# moves, the gate runs again against the marker itself. A compromised

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

  release:
    name: Auto-release (tag cut)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1522: the release IS the tag. Every push to main cuts an annotated
    # tag (latest tag + 1) on origin/main plus the GitHub Release — coalesced
    # to <=1 per 2h (pub.dev rate-limits publishes, ~12/day; hit on
    # 2026-07-18). ZERO commits land on main: the retired flow pushed a
    # 4-file 'chore(release):' bot commit (pubspec.yaml, CHANGELOG.md,
    # flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock}); the tag now drives everything and CI
    # stamps version/changelog into the STAGED publish tree at publish time.
    # The tag push rides the fa-release-bot App token because GITHUB_TOKEN
    # pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172);
    # the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no branch push), but
    # remains the release-path actor (gh-1402). Scheduled runs catch up
    # commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
      || github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))
    concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```

{"content":"## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```

version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

{"content":"## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

{"content":"## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
